text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1951234567 — policy-engine runtime error detected in smart-routing. Paging on-call. Affected: hosted inference routing (partial region loop). See /incidents/1951234567 for channel updates.

oncall-bot: Pager details: error rate spike + fallback churn observed for customers served from eu-west-1. Symptom: repeated fallback to small-quant model variant and increased 5xx.

alice gonzalez: i’m on it — looking at logs now. can someone confirm if any deploys happened to policy engine in last 30m?

benji: no deploys from eng-runtime in last hour. only config push at 17:02 which touched smart-routing ruleset (auto-rollout).

mira: I’m pulling the policy engine logs and trace. seeing repeated panics:

benji: ```
2026-11-03T17:15:22Z policy-engine[pid=2345]: panic: runtime error: invalid expression evaluation: nil pointer deref
#0 0x45b2c1 in eval.ExprEval
#1 0x45c9f0 in rules.Evaluate
#2 0x41208a in routing.DecideVariant
#3 0x401f0b in http.Handler

error context: rule_id=sr-eu-001, incoming={"customer":"acme","region":null,"latency_ms":12}
```

alice gonzalez: note: incoming.region is null a lot — some frontends didn't set region on older requests. rule references req.region directly.

eng-runtime: confirmed. rule sr-eu-001 expects req.region but some callers (legacy edge) send region as empty. expression has no null guard — that triggers panic in our evaluator.

charlie: that explains a loop: when Evaluate panics, the runtime falls back to next policy which in our routing stack toggles region->global and re-invokes policy in another region; then the policy tries to access region again -> repeated fallback and cross-region churn. customers see extra latency and model downgrade.

alice gonzalez: customer impact: several paying tenants in EU measuring 3x latency and dropped requests. support-bot: ticket spike for account acme and beta-retail.

support-bot: Generated tickets: TICK-4482, TICK-4483, TICK-4486 — assigned to support-swift.

mira: mitigation options: 1) hotfix policy evaluator to handle missing fields (catch panics) — needs code change + deploy (20-30m). 2) disable offending rule/safe-fallback to static mapping immediately via console (1-2m). 3) patch config to add null-coalesce guard in rule (fast but needs ruleset push).

alice gonzalez: do (2) now — disable sr-eu-001 and flip smart-routing -> static-routes for EU for the next 30m. I'll do canary in 1 region first.

benji: Command to run: `redwoodctl policies update sr-eu-001 --enabled=false` or via Console UI. mir a, can you prepare the static mapping?

mira: prepping static map: mapping eu -> eu-variant-v3 (same model as before but without dynamic routing). snippet: ```yaml
static_routes:
  - region: eu
    variant: eu-variant-v3
    priority: 10
```

eng-runtime: heads-up: disabling rule will stop the panic chain but keep an eye on latency — static routes may increase token-cost. also we should throttle retries to avoid cold-start thundering. setting retry-window to 30s.

alice gonzalez: done — disabled sr-eu-001 and applied static mapping to eu. monitoring now.

oncall-bot: Action log: sr-eu-001 disabled by alice gonzalez at 2026-11-03T17:19:10Z. static map applied.

benji: checking metrics — 17:20: latency trending down, 5xxs dropping. fallback churn rate reduced from ~120/min to <5/min.

charlie: can we also push a temporary guard rule that avoids referencing req.region directly? like `let r = req.region ?? "unknown"` — does rule language support that?

eng-runtime: current rule language supports `exists`/`has` checks. we can do `if has(req.region) && req.region == "eu" then ...` quick patch to ruleset would be safe. but i'm still going to own a small runtime patch to make evaluation robust to nils.

mira: i've queued a conservative ruleset patch with `has` guard and will push after we stabilize (ETA 10m).

alice gonzalez: oncall handoff plan: I'll monitor for 15m and then hand to benji for overnight. benji are you ok to take on-call follow-up?

benji: will take it. I'll coordinate incident writeup and postmortem. please tag eng-runtime and eng-sre for root cause.

sre-lead: from SRE standpoint — request: increase observability on policy eval failures (metric + alert) and add a circuit-breaker so policy-eval panics don't trigger downstream fallback loops. filing SRE task SR-559.

eng-runtime: assigned ENGRT-901 to add try/catch around eval and return structured error instead of panic. target hotfix: deploy to canary in 40m, full roll 2h. will also add defensive unit tests for missing fields.

support-bot: Notifying impacted customers with status update: "We have applied a temporary routing fix; engineering is investigating the root cause and will follow up."

charlie: any data loss or model-cache corruption risk? eng-runtime: no evidence of persistence corruption; only request-level panics.

alice gonzalez: recording timeline for postmortem:
- 17:02 config push touched sr-eu-001 (no immediate errors)
- 17:15 sudden error spike and routing panics start
- 17:17 automated paging (this thread)
- 17:19 rule disabled + static map applied (initial mitigation)
- 17:28 metrics recovered to baseline

benji: i'll start the incident doc and add ownerships. next steps: follow-up fix in runtime, stricter linting for new rules, and a deploy-gate to run rules conformance tests against a 'missing fields' harness.

oncall-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. P1 -> P2. Please file postmortem and link here when ready.

alice gonzalez: handing to benji now. thanks all. :thumbsup:
